text:
Which of the following statements are correct about $\mathrm{Zn},\mathrm{Cd}$ and $\mathrm{Hg}$ ?

A. They exhibit high enthalpy of atomization as the d-subshell is full.

B. $\mathrm{Zn}$ and $\mathrm{Cd}$ do not show variable oxidation state while $\mathrm{Hg}$ shows $+\mathrm{I}$ and $+\mathrm{II}$.

C. Compounds of $\mathrm{Zn},\mathrm{Cd}$ and $\mathrm{Hg}$ are paramagnetic in nature.

D. $\mathrm{Zn},\mathrm{Cd}$ and $\mathrm{Hg}$ are called soft metals.

Choose the most appropriate from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement A is incorrect: Zn, Cd and Hg have the lowest enthalpies of atomisation in their series, because the completely filled $(n-1)d^{10}$ subshell does not take part in metallic bonding.

Statement B is correct: Zn and Cd show only the +2 state, while Hg shows +1 (in $\mathrm{Hg}{}_{2}{}^{2+}$) as well as +2.

Statement C is incorrect: the $\mathrm{M}{}^{2+}$ ions are $d^{10}$, and in $\mathrm{Hg}{}_{2}{}^{2+}$ the two 6s electrons are paired in the Hg–Hg bond, so there are no unpaired electrons and the compounds are diamagnetic.

Statement D is correct: unlike the other transition metals, which are hard, Zn, Cd and Hg are soft metals (Hg is a liquid at room temperature).

The correct statements are B and D only.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Chromatographic technique/s based on the principle of differential adsorption is / are

A. Column chromatography

B. Thin layer chromatography

C. Paper chromatography

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Adsorption chromatography separates the components of a mixture by their differential adsorption on a solid adsorbent (the stationary phase).

In column chromatography the mixture moves down a column packed with an adsorbent such as alumina or silica gel; components adsorbed less strongly move faster, so they separate.

Thin layer chromatography uses a thin layer of adsorbent (silica gel or alumina) spread on a glass plate, so it is also adsorption chromatography.

Paper chromatography is partition chromatography: water held by the cellulose of the paper is the stationary phase, and separation depends on differential partitioning between this water and the mobile phase.

So only column chromatography and thin layer chromatography (A and B) are based on differential adsorption.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: Anomalous behavior of oxygen is due to its
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Oxygen, the first member of group 16, differs in many properties from the other members ($\mathrm{S}$, $\mathrm{Se}$, $\mathrm{Te}$, $\mathrm{Po}$).

This is due to its small atomic size and high electronegativity (about 3.5, next only to fluorine); the absence of $d$ orbitals in its valence shell also limits its covalency to four.

Because of its small size and high electronegativity, oxygen forms strong hydrogen bonds, so $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is a liquid while $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}$ is a gas.

For the same reason it forms $pπ$-$pπ$ multiple bonds, so oxygen exists as diatomic $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ while sulphur forms $\mathrm{S}_{8}$.

So the anomalous behaviour of oxygen is due to its small size and high electronegativity.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: Which one of the following will show geometrical isomerism?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Geometrical isomerism about the exocyclic C=C requires two different groups on each doubly bonded carbon.

In (A), the exocyclic carbon carries H and Br, and the ring carbon carries two different ring arms, one reaching the C-Br carbon after one $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ and the other after three $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ groups, so E and Z isomers exist.

In (B) and (C), the exocyclic carbon is $=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$, with two identical H atoms.

In (D), the 1,4-placement makes the two ring arms identical, so no geometrical isomers arise (the molecule is axially chiral instead).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The total number of molecules with zero dipole moment among $\mathrm{CH}_{4},\mathrm{BF}_{3},\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O},\mathrm{HF},\mathrm{NH}_{3},\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{SO}_{2}$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine which molecules have a zero dipole moment from the list provided, we need to consider their molecular geometry and symmetry. Molecules that are symmetrical often have zero dipole moment because the bond dipoles cancel each other out.

CO₂ (Carbon Dioxide): This molecule is linear in shape. The two opposing oxygen atoms pull equally on the carbon, canceling out the dipoles, resulting in a net dipole moment of zero.

CH₄ (Methane): Methane is tetrahedral and symmetrical, with all four hydrogen atoms equally spaced around the carbon atom. This symmetry leads to the cancellation of dipoles, giving a net dipole moment of zero.

BF₃ (Boron Trifluoride): This molecule is trigonal planar and symmetrical. The three fluorine atoms are arranged evenly around the central boron atom, causing the dipoles to cancel each other out, resulting in a zero dipole moment.

Therefore, the molecules with zero dipole moment among the list provided are CO₂, CH₄, and BF₃.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The following concentrations were observed at $500\mathrm{K}$ for the formation of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ from $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$. At equilibrium ; $[\mathrm{N}_{2}]=2\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{M},[\mathrm{H}_{2}]=3\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{M}$ and $[\mathrm{NH}_{3}]=1.5\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{M}$. text:
The half-life of radioisotope bromine - 82 is 36 hours. The fraction which remains after one day is $________$ $\times 10^{-2}$.

(Given antilog $0.2006=1.587$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Half life of bromine-82 $=36$ hours

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{t}_{1/2}=\dfrac{0.693}{\mathrm{K}} \\ \mathrm{K}=\dfrac{0.693}{36}=0.01925\mathrm{hr}^{-1} \\ 1^{\text{st}}\text{order rxn kinetic equation} \\ \mathrm{t}=\dfrac{2.303}{\mathrm{K}}\log \dfrac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{x}} \\ \log \dfrac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{x}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{t}\times \mathrm{K}}{2.303}(\mathrm{t}=1\text{day}=24\mathrm{hr}) \\ \log \dfrac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{x}}=\dfrac{24\mathrm{hr}\times 0.01925\mathrm{hr}^{-1}}{2.303} \\ \log \dfrac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{x}}=0.2006 \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{x}}=\mathrm{anti}\log (0.2006) \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{x}}=1.587 \\ \text{If}\mathrm{a}=1 \\ \dfrac{1}{1-\mathrm{x}}=1.587\Rightarrow 1-\mathrm{x}=0.6301=\text{Fraction remain} \\ \mathrm{after}\text{one day} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The total number of 'Sigma' and 'Pi' bonds in 2-formylhex-4-enoic acid is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
2-Formylhex-4-enoic acid is $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CHO})-\mathrm{COOH}$ ($\mathrm{C}{}_{7}\mathrm{H}{}_{10}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$); the formyl group is the aldehyde group $-\mathrm{CHO}$.


[IMG]

Every bond contains one $σ$ bond, and each double bond contains one $π$ bond in addition.

$σ$ bonds: 9 C–H (three on C-6, one each on C-5, C-4 and C-2, two on C-3 and one on the formyl carbon), 1 O–H, 6 C–C (five along the six-carbon chain and one to the formyl carbon) and 3 C–O (one in each C=O and the C–OH bond of the acid), so $9+1+6+3=19$.

$π$ bonds: one each in the C=C, the acid C=O and the aldehyde C=O, so 3.

Total $=19+3=22$.

Hence, the answer is 22.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The oxidation number of iron in the compound formed during brown ring test for NO${}_{3}^{-}$ ion is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the brown ring test, $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ reduces $\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}{}^{-}$ to NO in the presence of conc. $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$, and the NO binds to the excess $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$:

$\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}{}^{-}+3\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}+4\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\longrightarrow \mathrm{NO}+3\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}+\mathrm{NO}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{5}(\mathrm{NO})]{}^{2+}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

In the brown complex one electron passes from NO to iron, so the ligand is the nitrosonium ion $\mathrm{NO}{}^{+}$ (charge $+1$), and $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is neutral.

For the oxidation number $x$ of Fe:

$x+5(0)+(+1)=+2\Rightarrow x=+1$

Hence, the answer is 1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift
